solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bimbo not entirely in possession of bodybuilder

indicators.note: not entirely says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: a bimbo is an attractive but empty-headed woman, a dumb belle

explanation.surface: An airhead woman only half-owning a muscleman.
explanation.walkthrough: DUMB BELLE, a pretty but brainless woman, loses her final E. 'in possession of' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight lifted to build muscle; the equipment is a body builder in a punning sense.

clue.text: Stop believer embracing leader in Satan

indicators.note: embracing means the word for believer holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a deist believes in a creator God without revealed religion

indicators.note: leader in Satan points to the opening letter of that name

explanation.surface: An instruction for a believer to halt while hugging the Devil's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cease or refrain from doing something.

clue.text: Low luminescence primarily visible during hours of darkness?

definitions.text: Low luminescence primarily visible during hours of darkness?

parts.words: Low luminescence primarily visible during hours of darkness?
parts.note: a gentle, dim glow seen chiefly at night, given by the lunar body reflecting sunlight

explanation.walkthrough: The clue simply describes the soft light of the moon, seen mostly at night; 'Low' may also hint at MOO, the sound of a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar light is a faint glow that is mainly seen after dark.

clue.text: Mostly great exercise to have boy brought up like a man, perhaps?

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: great means big
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: Advice on boosting a boy's development with exercise to make him manly.
explanation.walkthrough: BI (most of BIG) plus PE, then LAD turned upward to give DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on two legs is a trait of humans, so a man is an example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Red line on square running vertically

indicators.note: running vertically in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom up
on in the order means the line follows the square

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A red line drawn upright across a square.
explanation.walkthrough: NINE followed by L gives NINEL, which reads upward in the grid as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Red is a communist; the Bolshevik leader is the archetypal one.

clue.text: We're asking for financial support, being behind

definitions.meaning: a plea of 'give us money' split as two words
the anatomical term for the base or rear part of a hollow organ

explanation.surface: A charity appeal from people who are behind on their bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is a request for money; whole, it is the medical name for an organ's bottom part.

clue.text: Best immoral activity starts in June, with dropping of skirts — perfect!

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the month's middle
dropping the skirts removes the outer letters of the month, leaving its centre

parts.note: to top is to best, outdo

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the two words immoral and activity

explanation.surface: A racy tale of immoral fun one June, when skirts came off and all was perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is a verb here (to outdo), and 'starts' covers both 'immoral' and 'activity'; 'dropping of skirts' strips June's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ideally perfect, in the manner of an imagined flawless society.

clue.text: Valley bleak at its nadir, soulless thing

parts.note: a dale is a valley

indicators.note: nadir is the lowest point, so in a down clue it is the bottom letter of bleak

explanation.surface: A desolate valley at its lowest point, an empty soulless place.
explanation.walkthrough: DALE then K, the last letter of 'bleak'. The answer is the robotic villain from the British science-fiction series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: This robotic alien of Doctor Who is a pitiless machine-encased creature, seen as without a soul.

clue.text: Girl pens that article that's so long

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the girl's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl writes an article so lengthy it seems to have no end.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese farewell, used in English like 'goodbye' or 'see you'.

clue.text: Those still safeguarding last of ancient laws

indicators.note: safeguarding means holding protectively, so the letter sits within

parts.note: statues stand still

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of ancient

explanation.surface: Old statues preserving the final traces of ancient laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: written laws passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Certainly falling over backwards about one-legged giant, one rolling in the aisles?

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the rest
falling over backwards says the word is turned end to end

parts.note: certainly means yes
moving on one leg is hopping
a troll is a giant of folklore

explanation.surface: Someone collapsing with laughter at a one-legged giant, rolling in the aisles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling over backwards' turns the word for 'Certainly' end to end, giving SEY, and 'about' wraps that around the giant who hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket cart wheels along the aisles, punning on the laughter idiom.

clue.text: Sultan leaves home

parts.note: salad is made of leaves
at home is in

explanation.surface: A ruler departs for his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is a noun: salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Named example: the 12th-century Muslim leader who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: Figure pressing simple bloke to become more complex

indicators.note: pressing means squeezing round, so the number holds the other word

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
a hick is an unsophisticated country fellow

explanation.surface: A number squeezes a naive man until things grow complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: when a plot thickens it grows more intricate.

clue.text: Personal restriction legit — I'm a crackpot!

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so these letters are put in a mad new order

explanation.surface: Someone insists their own curb is legitimate, then admits being a crank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap on how old a person may be, a restriction applied to individuals.

clue.text: A tide moving through the sea, settled

indicators.note: through means the shuffled letters run inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: moving means the letters of a tide are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A tide flowing through the Mediterranean, then calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: resolved a dispute by acting as a go-between.

clue.text: Land in King Lear, where every second counts

indicators.note: every second means take the even-placed letters of the phrase in King Lear

explanation.surface: A territory in Shakespeare's tragedy where timing is crucial.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a West African country, a land in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: River bird welcoming swallow

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the bird holds the verb

parts.note: the grouse is a game bird
to swallow is to eat

explanation.surface: A river bird greets a swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' is the verb, not the bird. The answer is a river in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Named example: a long river of East Anglia flowing to the Wash.

clue.text: Duck covering wet ground, keeping another duck drier

indicators.note: covering means the duck wraps around the inner letters

parts.note: the teal is a duck

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the zero
ground as in crushed means the letters of wet are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck on wet ground protects another duck that is drying off.
explanation.walkthrough: TWE (from 'wet', 'ground') holds O, giving TOWE, inside TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for wiping dishes, something that dries.

clue.text: Further context rarely entertains

indicators.note: entertains means the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: Additional background seldom amuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: additional, more than needed.

clue.text: After spiking drink, missionary appears

indicators.note: spiking means lacing, so the drink has the word put inside it

parts.note: ale is a drink
post means after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: Once someone laces a drink, a preacher shows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an early Christian sent out to spread the faith.

clue.text: Poor grade is a bloomer — a calamity!

parts.note: D is a poor exam grade
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A low mark is a blunder, something awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a catastrophe or great misfortune.

clue.text: Needing first from Surrey, one brushed up on history finally, so happy

indicators.note: first from takes the opening letter of Surrey

parts.note: a quiff is a hairstyle brushed up off the forehead

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of history

explanation.surface: A cheerful Surrey student swots up on history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy' here means pleasantly tipsy, a British colloquial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for slightly drunk, the tipsy sense of merry.

clue.text: Sampling the sea air, perhaps, conked out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone taking the sea air who has simply passed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship's open deck is one place to breathe the sea air, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Into endless Spanish food, I love cold pudding

indicators.note: into means the following letters go inside the shortened food
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: tapas are Spanish snacks
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A diner fond of tapas declares a love of chilled dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a milk pudding of starch pearls from cassava.

clue.text: John's secret

definitions.meaning: the john is slang for a lavatory
private, as in ... to a secret

explanation.definitionFit: It is an old word for an outside lavatory and also means sharing secret knowledge.

clue.text: Likes, for a start, to fill belly with huge amount — does he?

definitions.text: Likes, for a start, to fill belly with huge amount — does he?

indicators.note: to fill means the letter goes inside the word for belly

parts.note: the gut is the belly

indicators.note: for a start takes the first letter of Likes

parts.note: a ton is a huge amount

explanation.surface: A question about someone who loves stuffing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the wordplay and also a description of the greedy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater is one who likes to stuff his stomach with masses of food.

clue.text: Absurd sentimentality about antipodean nation

indicators.note: about means the gooey word goes around the country letters

parts.note: goo is mawkish sentiment
NZ is New Zealand

explanation.surface: Ridiculous sentimental gush about New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for bizarre or wildly unconventional, as in gonzo journalism.

clue.text: Something to play after card game, having led an unlikely suit

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: unlikely signals the letters of led an are in an improbable order

parts.note: a flute is an instrument to play

explanation.surface: After a card game someone plays music, having led an improbable suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: whistle and flute rhymes with suit. 'suit' tempts as a card suit but is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang, often shortened to whistle, for a man's suit of clothes.

clue.text: Amateurs, namely, maladjusted

indicators.note: maladjusted means badly arranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Amateurs, that is to say, are badly adjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: non-professionals, people without specialist training.

clue.text: Said to be completely exhausted in the days before Easter

indicators.note: said to be signals the phrase is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: completely is wholly and exhausted is weak

explanation.surface: Someone described as totally worn out in the run-up to Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian calendar's week leading up to Easter Sunday.
